current.text: He is a rookie and was the number one overall pick. Washington is building around him as its centerpiece.
He is projected to start at small forward. He may also play shooting guard or power forward depending on the lineup.
Trae Young and Anthony Davis are expected to take preferred touches, so his shots and usage will be much lower than his 35% summer league usage.
Washington may bring him along slowly. He could play around 28 minutes a night early on instead of 34 or more.
Experts do not expect his fantasy value to come together in year one. They expect bigger usage in years two and three.

Experts agree his market price is too high. A Yahoo rank of 93 and an ADP in the 70s are called overdrafts. Category projections range from outside the top 100 to about 180th. The newest note says he will not be rosterable to start the season. One expert calls him fine around pick 120.
In auction he is seen as a 1 USD player. He went for 4 USD in a mock draft, which the expert called too much.
He had 5 steals and 3 blocks in two summer league games, which he does not usually do.
If his summer league defensive stats stick, his value moves up.
Washington is trying to compete and is projected near .500 and in the play-in mix. Late-season resting and minutes cuts are not expected.
Head coach Brian Keefe is under pressure to win this season.
Washington has a deep group of wings and guards, with a 10 or 11 man rotation expected.

durable.text: He is a volume scorer who gets to the rim and the free throw line at will. He drew about 7 free throws per game in summer league, as he did at BYU, and shot 89% at the rim.
He shot badly in summer league: 1 for 11 from three and 39% from the field.
Most experts call him a poor shooter with low three-point volume, below average free throws and concerning shot selection. One expert calls his shooting fine.
Experts call his steals and blocks poor and his defense a concern.
Experts disagree on his passing. Some call his ball skills, passing and pick and roll play above average for his size. Others call his passing unclear or not strong.
His rebounds are okay but not high.
Turnovers are his weakest category and are weak for a forward.
Experts see the weakest category league profile among the top four rookies. He is worth more in points leagues than in category leagues.
Experts see a strong long-term floor because of his size, usage, shot creation and handle.

note: The market has him near rank 90 (Yahoo value 5 USD, ESPN average cost 5.7 USD). Experts put him at about 1 USD, and his projected line is close to neutral everywhere except points (+0.8 z) and turnovers (-0.8 z). Let someone else pay for the No. 1 pick name. He only makes sense as a 1 to 2 USD bench piece for a punt TO build. Early in the season, check his minutes (28 or 34 plus), his shot share next to Trae Young and Anthony Davis, and whether his summer league steals and blocks hold up.
